$comment: Resolution JSONB classification v1 (plan 8261645, Track D / package D2).
Purpose: when the KG projection is rebuilt, every governed JSONB column in
the resolution schema must have a declared class, so that JSONB storage
cannot silently erase governed keys or temporal semantics.
Class precedence (highest first): authority > queryable_identity > lineage
> projection > payload_only. A column takes the HIGHEST class any of its
No migration is applied by this file. It is a classification, not a DDL.

payload_only.definition: Free-form content carried for humans/consumers; never queried as identity, never authoritative.
payload_only.projection_rule: may be projected verbatim as payload; must not be indexed as a governed key
payload_only.promotion_rule: promotion to a higher class requires an architect ruling and a migration

queryable_identity.definition: Contains keys used to identify or join an entity (canonical keys, subject/object refs).
queryable_identity.projection_rule: every governed key must be reachable as a typed projection column; JSONB-only storage is not sufficient
queryable_identity.promotion_rule: adding a governed key requires declaring it in this file before first use

lineage.definition: Points at the origin of a claim (source records, evidence refs, verification summaries).
lineage.projection_rule: project as edges with provenance (source_authority, source_record_id, fingerprint); never flatten into text

authority.definition: Carries or binds an authority decision (acknowledgements, constraints, dispositions).
authority.projection_rule: project as a governed node; JSONB is storage only — the authoritative record stays in its owning schema
authority.promotion_rule: never inferred from payload shape; requires an authority_ref

projection.definition: Materialized view/snapshot data produced by another owner.
projection.projection_rule: recomputable and disposable; must carry the projection generation and recorded_at, and must never be read back as authority

columns.rationale: Scope references bound an assessment to the assets it touched; projected as edges.
columns.temporal_semantics: none in-column; validity carried by assessment row columns

columns.rationale: Human-readable reasoning; not a join key and not an authority record.
Free-form array for implementers.
Illustrative code; explicitly not a contract of record.
Narrative design notes.
GOVERNED KEYS: identity attributes used to recognise the asset. JSONB must not be the only home of a governed key.
governed_keys: asset identity keys as declared by semantics canonical_asset_id
columns.temporal_semantics: identity is time-independent; asset validity/supersession is expressed by columns/edges, not by JSONB

columns.rationale: Identifies the claim subject; used to join claims to assets.
Identifies/characterises the claim object; part of the claim identity when it carries an id.
columns.temporal_semantics: none; claim timing is carried by the row

columns.rationale: Summarises which evidence verified a claim; lineage for the projection.
columns.temporal_semantics: verification instant must be a column, not a JSONB field

columns.rationale: Origin pointer for evidence; becomes a provenance edge.
columns.temporal_semantics: valid_from/valid_until/recorded_on_dt on the evidence row; never inside source_ref

columns.rationale: Evidence body as produced by the caller.
Caller metadata; not queried as identity.
Derived harvest representation.
columns.temporal_semantics: harvest window is carried by row/columns

columns.rationale: Describes the producing run (model, batch); lineage for the harvest.
columns.temporal_semantics: run start/end must be columns if they are governed

columns.rationale: Free-form metadata.
Criteria rendered for consumers; the authoritative plan text stays with the plan owner (conduit).
Free-form plan metadata.
Observation body. Note: some rows carry decision-relevant facts; those become governed only by promoting a governed key, never by reading payload ad hoc.
Captured representation metadata used to recompute disagreement projections.
columns.temporal_semantics: representation capture time must remain a column

columns.rationale: Rendered criteria; authoritative requirement content lives with the requirement owner.
Snapshot of specification items; recomputable and disposable.
columns.temporal_semantics: snapshot generation + recorded_at must be present

columns.rationale: Properties attached to a graph edge as evidence for a relation.
Carries the governing context under which the WR was admitted; treated as authority-bearing metadata, not free text.
columns.temporal_semantics: as-of/effective instants must remain columns where they govern

columns.rationale: Admission constraints are binding; a constraint that only exists inside JSONB is unenforceable.
Edge decorations; relation identity is carried by the edge columns.

invariants: No governed key may exist ONLY inside a JSONB column: every key listed under governed_keys must be reachable from a typed column or a declared projection rule.
JSONB storage never relocates temporal semantics: valid_from/valid_until/recorded_on_dt/recorded_until_dt stay first-class columns.
A JSONB value that references another authority must name a member of the closed authority set; unknown authorities are rejected (see schemas/decision-b-freeze/jsonb_contract_test.py).
Class assignment is conservative: where two classes are defensible, the higher class wins.
Reclassification is a new classification_version, never an in-place edit.
open_questions: resolution.observation.payload contains decision-relevant facts in seeded rows (e.g. candidate_compile_failure, representation_disagreement). If the projection needs those as graph claims, promote named keys under queryable_identity rather than parsing payload generically.

resolution.work_request.context/constraints are classified authority here; if the owning service treats them as advisory, an architect ruling should downgrade them explicitly rather than leaving the classification ambiguous.
